title: Tenant Enablement Sprint Template & OKR Alignment for Private Instances
creator: Nora Patel
description:
Problem: Customers deploying Redwood Private instances have variable onboarding velocity and inconsistent success signals. We need a prescriptive sprint template and OKR mapping that PMs, Solutions, and Eng can use to bring an enterprise tenant from contract to production in a predictable cadence while preserving safety and compatibility checks.

Goal: Create a lightweight, repeatable sprint template (6-week cadence + acceptance gates) that: 1) maps to measurable OKRs, 2) surfaces required infra/eng tasks and checkpoints, 3) provides a governance/signoff matrix (security, infra, legal), and 4) includes a small set of telemetry signals for go/no-go.

This ticket scopes the PM deliverable (template + OKR mapping + example run) and the cross-functional coordination plan to pilot with 2 customers in Q2.
acceptance_criteria: A templated sprint plan (Markdown + Confluence page) that includes milestones, role responsibilities, acceptance gates, and checklist
OKR mapping document: which product/eng metrics change maps to outcome metrics (time-to-prod, failure-budget usage, first-ML-inference-run)
Two pilot-ready runbooks for different customer archetypes (on-prem air-gapped, cloud VPC)
Stakeholder signoff captured from Security, Solutions, Runtime Eng, and Customer Success
Telemetry workbook with 5 signals wired to the console dashboard (time-to-first-api, infra-failures, deploy-rollback-rate, latency-benchmarks, KB of customer-specific config drift)
milestones: 2026-02-22: Draft sprint template and checklist complete
2026-03-01: Internal review with Security & Solutions (feedback round)
2026-03-08: Pilot runbook variants authored for air-gapped and VPC
2026-03-15: OKR mapping and telemetry workbook completed
2026-03-31: Confluence + Shareable artifact published; handoff to Solutions for pilots
risks: Unresolved runtime upgrade compatibility could block pilot tenants
Security review may require additional hardening for air-gapped installs
Telemetry collection for on-prem customers requires a lightweight opt-in agent; scope creep risk
Resource contention: Solutions engineering availability during pilot windows
metrics: % of pilot tenants achieving all gates without >1 rollback (target 80%)
Average infra failure rate during enablement (target <0.5 per tenant-week)
Customer satisfaction NPS for enablement experience (target >= +30)
First inference call latency within expected SLA band for dedicated capacity
notes: This is intentionally prescriptive and narrow: focus on the enablement path from signed contract to first production traffic for tenants on Private/VPC or on-prem package. Avoid building a full automation product in this scope; we want a template and a small set of runbooks we can reuse and iterate on. Coordinate with Runtime Eng on compatibility gates and with Security on minimal required checklist items for air-gapped installs.
